page: Microsoft Azure M32-8ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. The hardware configuration includes 875.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 109.38 GB per core. Additionally, it features 1049 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear tradeoff between massive memory capacity and processing throughput. The CPU performance is generally modest, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core benchmarks falling into the poor and weak categories respectively. Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores also reflect this lower-tier compute profile. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block speed of 38.73 GB/sec and a write large block speed of 31.04 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations, such as the Passmark database test and Redis SET operations, fall into the bottom 25% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M32-8ms is designed for workloads that require massive memory density rather than raw compute power. The high ratio of 875.0 GB of RAM to only 8 vCPUs makes it a specialized option where licensing costs tied to CPU core counts can be minimized while maintaining a very large in-memory footprint. This profile is suitable for large in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications with massive memory requirements but low-to-moderate parallel processing demands.
description: Microsoft Azure M32-8ms is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 1049 GB of local storage, and an exceptionally large memory capacity of 875.0 GB, providing 109.38 GB of RAM per core. Benchmark data indicates a clear tradeoff: while memory capacity is massive, compute performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores falling into the bottom 10% to 25% ranges. Memory write bandwidth is average at 31.04 GB/sec, but read bandwidth and database operations are lower-tier. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high memory density with minimal CPU core licensing requirements. It is best suited for large in-memory databases, caching systems, and memory-intensive enterprise applications with moderate processing needs.
